post.summary: MCP server over HTTP (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0) — plugs into the client with nothing to install.
post.description:
The tools are the operations of this same catalog; the MCP has no backend of its own. `GET /mcp` returns the server card.
Returns: JSON-RPC 2.0 response (`initialize`, `tools/list` or `tools/call`).
Credentials go in the usual headers (X-Guest-Token, Authorization, X-PAYMENT) and are forwarded to the API.
An exhausted quota comes back as a 402 with accepts[] inside the tool result — pay and repeat.

get.summary: The public mosaic: paginated search of the catalog's listings, the lower-signal tail last.
get.description:
`live` listings first and the `low` tail (few stars or no clear license) after them in every order — `low=0` leaves the tail out. To walk everything, follow `next`: without `q` it is a cursor (`next_cursor`, keyset on the order's index) and has no ceiling; every listing also has an HTML page at `/l/:id` and the shards of `/sitemap-listings.xml` list them all. `q` runs on a full-text index (FTS5, bm25) kept in the same transaction as every text write. With `q` and `low=0`, `low_count` says how many `low` listings the filter left out — LIKE with a cap of 200. The query is mapped onto kind/topic/transport filters unless `interpret=0`.
Returns: { items[{id,kind,category,name,tagline,body,url,status,origin,origin_id,install,source,transporte,ns,versao,oficial_status,repo_host,topico,linguagem,licenca,repo_topics,repo_slug,stars,forks,prs_abertos,pushed_at,repo_estado,likes,comments,visits,created_at,updated_at,mine,api,go,comments_api,readme_api?,historico?,readme_fonte?,readme_bytes,readme_sha,readme_em,payload}], limit, offset, next_offset, next_cursor, next, low_count, low_capped, low_included, interpretacao, api }

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text over the name, the tagline, the description, the origin identifier and the README excerpt: every word (up to six, 2+ letters, accents ignored) must match; ranked by bm25 with the name weighing most (10), then tagline (5), identifier (3), description (2), README excerpt (1); ties by stars. Kind, topic and transport words become filters. The `low` tail is in the same index.

parameters.name: interpret
parameters.description: `0` disables query understanding and searches the raw string.

parameters.description: Which kind of resource to fetch.

schema.default: relevancia when q is set, recent otherwise

parameters.description: Result order. parameters.name: low
parameters.description: `0` leaves the `low` tail out; by default it comes after the `live` listings in every order.

parameters.name: cursor

post.summary: Registers an MCP server, a skill or a plugin in the catalog. It comes in as `pending`.
post.description:
Automatic review approves supported low-risk MCP listings; uncertain cases wait for a person. Poll `status_api` (`GET /api/listings/:id/status`, no credential) to learn the decision. A person or agent can submit without an account. While billing is off, no payment is required. Each owner can submit once a day and keep up to three submissions in the queue. For a skill, provide its SKILL.md URL. If agent billing is enabled, the reference price is US$ 0.10 per submission, paid through x402 or prepaid credit. The service checks the body and quota before charging. An invalid body returns 400; an exhausted quota returns 429.
Returns: { ok, id, status, status_api }

url.description: MCP endpoint, SKILL.md URL, the plugin's repository or the OKF bundle's `index.md`. For an OKF bundle on a domain you control, `POST /api/okf/ping` is free.

name.description: Display name; without it, taken from the source.

tagline.description: One line saying what it is for.

category.description: Category so the listing shows up under the right filter.

ok.description: Always `true` when the request went in.

status.description: Always `pending`: everything goes through the queue before turning live.

status_api.description: Where to poll for the review, with no credential (`GET /api/listings/:id/status`).

402.description: Quota exceeded. The response carries `accepts[]` (x402, USDC on Base): pay and repeat the same call with `X-PAYMENT`.

429.description: 1 per day, at most 3 pending — applies to both doors, and is checked before charging.

502.description: The payment settled and the write failed. The body carries `transaction`: keep it and talk to support.

get.summary: The feed index: RSS, Atom and JSON feeds, OPML reading lists and sites that only become a feed through a bridge.
get.description:
Find feeds by text, format, language and availability. Filter and text search run in the SAME full-text query: values inside one parameter are OR'd, different parameters are AND'd. Without `q` the order is by newest in the index (`recentes`) and `next_cursor` is a keyset — follow `next` to walk everything. With `q` the order is relevance and paging is by `offset`. We index and link; the feeds belong to whoever publishes them.
Returns: { items[{id,kind,dominio,url,nome,descricao,tipo,audio,video,comunidade,comunidades,ano,recursos,densidade,itens,saude,pais,site_titulo,site_descricao,site_nome,site_og,site_og_alt,site_cor,site_idioma,idioma_bandeira,icone,imagem,ultimo_post,posts_24h,posts_7d,posts_30d,posts_dias,posts_no_feed,posts_parcial,atividade_em,pagina,api}], limit, offset, next_cursor, next_offset, next, sort, api }

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text over the feed name, its description and the domain. Every word must match; accents are ignored.

parameters.name: origem
parameters.description: Where the record comes from. Comma-separated values are OR'd.

parameters.name: tipo
parameters.description: Feed format. Comma-separated values are OR'd.

parameters.name: midia
parameters.description: Enclosures the feed carries — this is how you find podcasts and video feeds.

parameters.name: comunidade
parameters.description: Community the publisher belongs to, as the source's bitmask declares it.

parameters.name: recurso
parameters.description: Namespace seen in the feed: `content` means the whole post travels in the feed, `itunes`/`podcast` mean podcast metadata, `slash` means comment counts.

parameters.name: lista
parameters.description: For OPML lists only: how the list presents itself.

parameters.name: ano
parameters.description: Year of the newest item the crawler saw. `0` means the source never dated the content. It is a year, not a moving window: the value never drifts.

parameters.name: saude
parameters.description: What our own check saw: `ok` answered, `erro` refused or timed out, `sumiu` returned 404/410. A feed not checked yet matches none of them.

parameters.name: pais
parameters.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 of the IP that serves the host, lowercase or uppercase, resolved in the same check.

parameters.name: dominio
parameters.description: Exact domain — the fastest way to ask whether a site has a feed.

parameters.name: idioma
parameters.description: Language of the site's home page, two or three letters: `pt` matches `pt` and `pt-br`.

parameters.name: imagem
parameters.description: `1` keeps only feeds whose site has a stored preview image (`imagem` is not empty) — the list that looks like a wall of link cards.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Result order. `recentes` is insertion in the index (what just arrived). `postando` is the newest post first, read from the feed itself (feeds without a dated post are left out). `frequentes` is most posts in the last 30 days first (same). `densidade` is how much item text discovery found — the closest thing to 'this feed has substance'. `dominio` is A–Z by site.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from `next_cursor` (orders `recentes`, `densidade` and `dominio`). A cursor from another order restarts at the first page.

get.summary: One post of a feed, with the body — the author's HTML and the same text in Markdown.

Two bodies for the same post, both from the copy we stored when we READ the feed — a request never fetches the site: `conteudo_html` keeps the author's formatting through an allowlist (only known tags and attributes survive; script, style, iframe and event handlers are dropped with their content), and `conteudo` is the same text as Markdown — the shape an agent usually wants. post.summary: Submits OKF bundles from a domain you control, using the IndexNow protocol.
post.description:
No account, no payment: ownership is proved by a key file on the host, exactly as IndexNow does it. Host `https://<host>/<key>.txt` containing the key (or point `keyLocation` at another path on the SAME host), then send the bundle URLs. We answer **202**: the key has not been checked yet. Verification and reading happen on our collector, never at the edge — so nothing is published, and no URL of yours is fetched, before the key matches. Re-sending a URL is how you say the bundle changed; it goes back in line to be re-read. At most 100 URLs per request and 200 per host per UTC day. The same queue is served by `POST https://okfindex.com/api/ping`, the index's own home — search, bundle cards and statistics live there.
Returns: { ok, estado, recebidos, chave_em }

urlList.description: Bundle `index.md` URLs. https, on `host`, ending in .md. No fixed path: the spec defines no discovery convention.

estado.description: Always `pendente`: the key has not been checked yet.

recebidos.description: How many distinct URLs entered the queue.

chave_em.description: Where we will look for the key file. Check it if you are unsure.

400.description: Malformed body, `host`/`key` invalid or `urlList` missing.

422.description: A URL is not https, is not .md, or does not belong to `host` — `keyLocation` on another host too.

nome.description: Name at the source, up to 300 characters.

visto_em.description: When the collector last wrote this item (ISO 8601).

agentes_com_skills.description: Agents whose card lists at least one skill.

bruto_por_fonte.description: Every source of the collector, the MCP indexes included, largest first.

acervo_por_kind.description: The size of `/api/a2a/acervo` per kind, largest first.

coleta.description: The last round of each source, by source id.

itens.description: Raw records kept from it.

credito.description: Credit and license of an A2A source; `null` for an MCP index (`/api/indices` credits it).

itens.description: Items of this kind.

no_catalogo.description: Items of this kind that the catalog already lists.

itens.description: Items read in that round.

novos.description: Items seen for the first time in it.

mudados.description: Items whose raw record changed in it.

ms.description: How long the round took, in milliseconds.

http.description: `200` when the round succeeded; when it failed, the source's HTTP status, or `0` if it never answered.

erro.description: Why the last round failed (`HTTP 503`, a timeout…); `null` when it succeeded.

proxima_em.description: When the next round is due (ISO 8601).

RodadaDaColetaA2A.description: The last collection round of one source on the index host.

fontes.description: Each source with its last batch and the count it brought.

falhas.description: Import failures not yet marked as seen.

orcamento.description: Today's publication budget (UTC day): `total`, `catalogo` (the catalog slice) and `okf` (the OKF slice), each with `usados` (rows actually written, as D1 counts them: row, key and every index entry, reconciled after each batch), `reservado` (the estimate charged before writing; `reservado / usados` is how inflated the estimate is) and `teto`; `classes` (catalogo, okf, fatos, readmes, fts) with today's `itens`, `reservado`, `linhas` (rows the database actually wrote) and `media` (real rows per item over the last days, the number the estimate now uses; null without history); plus `dia`.

Carga.description: The state of the catalog's load sources — where the listings come from and when they came.

prefs.description: The stored preferences, as the interface wrote them. `{}` when nothing was ever stored.

ok.description: Always `true` — failure comes as a 4xx/5xx status, not as `ok:false`.

Ok.description: Write confirmation with no body of its own to return.

provider.description: Always `x402` — the only billing protocol accepted.

mode.description: Seller mode: `live` charges for real, `dev` lets calls through unpaid.

network.description: USDC network: `base` in production, `base-sepolia` in staging.

chain_id.description: EVM chain ID of the network above, so the wallet signs on the right chain.

homolog.description: Staging seam on: the loop can be closed without spending USDC.

dev_gate.description: A homologation credential is configured; this grants no access.

facilitator.description: URL of the facilitator that verifies and settles the payment.

asset_address.description: USDC contract on the network above.

wallets.description: Links to wallets that speak x402 (metamask, coinbase, base_app).

prices.description: What each paid action costs, in USD.

listing_agent_usd.description: Reference price per agent submission. It is not charged while billing is off.

Precos.description: Prices in force, in dollars. Read them here, not from the documentation.

today_contacts.description: Contact messages received today. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: contact does not leave without a token.

days.description: One record per day of the window, with the counts of each metric.

usage.description: Usage per product resource — here, listings created through the surface (origin community); the registry's own catalog load does not count as usage.

financeiro.description: Aggregate of the day: `hoje_usd`, `hoje_count`, `rede`. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: money does not leave without a token; the full series is `payments`.

Metricas.description: 7-day panel. `payments` only shows with the operator token and only on Base mainnet.

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page; `null` when there is no more (or past the 1000 cap).

next.description: Absolute URL of the next page, same filters; follow it until it comes back `null`.

PaginaDeBundles.description: A page of the index. No `total`: counting on every search would cost a scan without changing any decision — `GET /api/okf/stats` has the totals.

id.description: Bundle id; the key across the whole API.

name.description: Title of the root `index.md`; `owner/repo · dir` when it has none or the title is a listing heading (`Files`, `Index`).

tagline.description: One line from the frontmatter `description`; empty when the author gave none.

description.description: Body of the root `index.md`, capped at 1000 characters.

okf_version.description: The `okf_version` the bundle declares (0.1 and 0.2 coexist).

concepts.description: How many linked entries the root index lists.

concept_list.description: The entries the root lists, in order, up to 24 — read from the indexed body, so a very long root is cut.

type.description: The `type` declared in the root frontmatter, when any.

index_url.description: The root `index.md`, raw — what you hand to an agent.

page_url.description: The page a human opens: the file on GitHub, or the bundle URL on its site.

source.description: Provenance and location of the bundle.

repo.description: Repository signal; `null` for bundles served by a domain.

indexed_at.description: When the bundle entered the index, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` UTC.

updated_at.description: When its indexed content last changed, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` UTC.

api.description: Absolute URL of this bundle's card.

Bundle.description: One OKF bundle: a markdown tree whose root `index.md` carries `okf_version`.

name.description: Link text as written in the root index.

url.description: Absolute URL of the entry, resolved against the root; a directory link gets its `index.md`.

summary.description: Text after the link on the same line; empty when the index has none.

Concept.description: One entry the root `index.md` lists: a concept file or a subdirectory of the bundle.

via.description: How it got in: the GitHub sweep or an IndexNow ping.

url.description: The repository (GitHub) or the site root (domain).

host.description: Hostname of `url`; empty when it cannot be parsed.

dir.description: Directory of the bundle inside the repository (empty at the root).

path.description: Path of the root `index.md` inside the repository.

BundleSource.description: Where a bundle comes from and how it entered the index.

state.description: Repository state as classified by the enricher (active, stalled, archived, gone).

RepoSignal.description: Repository signal collected by the enricher — GitHub bundles only.

by_origin.description: `{github, domain}`: live bundles found by the sweep and submitted by domains.

by_version.description: Live bundles per declared `okf_version`, most common first (up to 12).

by_type.description: Declared root types, up to 12; roots need not declare a type.

by_license.description: Repository licenses, up to 12; absent license is unknown.

by_language.description: Live bundles per repository language, most common first (up to 12); domain bundles have none.

last_update.description: Newest `updated_at` among live bundles, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` UTC.

IndexStats.description: Size of the index by provenance, the facets a search can filter by, and when it last changed.

v.description: The stored facet value or the concept-count band.

Faceta.description: One value of a facet and how many live bundles carry it.

historico.description: Newest first, at most 5: `{ em, tipo, de?, para? }` — `tipo` is `abandono` (no push for 12 months), `sumiu`, `renomeado`, `readme_mudou` or `manifesto_mudou`; `de`/`para` only for the state events.

ttl_s.description: Edge cache life of the slice, in seconds.

Historico.description: The repository's timeline behind a listing: the last events derived from continuous collection (ROADMAP-MAT F7).

truncado.description: More listings have counters than the 20,000 returned.

itens.description: One entry per listing with any counter: `id`, `likes`, `comments`, `visits`.

ok.description: Always `true` when there is a snapshot.

EstadoFila.description: The snapshot of the enrichment queue: how many listings have been checked and what is known about them.

vencidos.description: With an expired check, waiting for a new pass.

estados.description: Count per `repo_estado`: ativo, parado, arquivado, renomeado, sumiu.

motivos.description: Count per reason the listing is in the state it is in.

RetratoFila.description: Counters of the enrichment queue, pushed by the robot that checks the repositories.

total.description: Published items across topics (an item in two topics counts once).

atualizado_em.description: When the publisher generated this index (ISO 8601).

topicos.description: The topics, in the publisher's order.

inscricao.description: `{ aberta }`: `true` when `POST /api/briefings/subscribe` takes new subscriptions; until then it answers 503.

IndiceDosBriefings.description: Every topic with its count, the newest items across all of them and whether email subscriptions are open.

descricao.description: What the topic covers, in English (`en`) and Portuguese (`pt`).

api.description: Absolute URL of the topic in this API.

pagina.description: Absolute URL of the topic's HTML page.

TopicoDosBriefings.description: A topic: one public bookmark folder, with its count.

id.description: Id of the saved post on X; the item's key across topics.

slug.description: Topic the item was published under (its first topic).

autor.description: Handle of the post's author, with `@`.

post.description: Address of the post on X.

fonte.description: The main source the post cites (`url`, with `titulo` and `site` when known); `null` when the post is the source.

tipo.description: What the source is, by rule over its address.

previa.description: The source page's own preview: `titulo`, `site`, `imagem` (our WebP copy at `/briefings/img/<file>`, or `null`) and `generica` (`true` when the image is the site's logo, the same in many items).

resumo.description: What the source is, in one or two sentences, in English (`en`) and Portuguese (`pt`).

importa.description: Why an engineer should care, in English (`en`) and Portuguese (`pt`).

filtros.description: The filters in effect (`topico`, `tipo`), only values that exist.

itens.description: The items of this page, newest first; an item in two topics appears once.

PaginaDeBriefings.description: A slice of every published item by topic and source type, 20 per page, with the counts for each filter.

descricao.description: What the topic covers, in English (`en`) and Portuguese (`pt`).

paginas.description: How many pages the topic has.

itens.description: The items of this page.

TopicoDoBriefing.description: One topic, 20 items per page, newest first.

enabled.description: Present in public discovery; false means no purchases.

message.description: Next action in the requested language.

auto_renew.description: False: the client explicitly buys another package.

unit.description: catalog_read: one successful catalog response, at most 1 MiB.

products.description: Data indexes sharing the same package.

method.description: HTTP method for the explicit package purchase: POST.

status.description: GET with X-API-Pass checks the private purchase status.

instructions.description: Generate and retain the pass before payment.

client.description: Auditable ES module client; orchestrates purchase and data retry with caller-owned wallet and durable state.

guide.description: Client setup, explicit budget, recovery and data value.

purchase_requires_authority.description: The client needs an explicit spending budget.

retry_same_pass.description: Persist the pass and original signed proof before submitting.

on_unknown_payment.description: Query the purchase or reconcile the original proof; never sign again automatically.

active.description: Has credit and has not expired.

paid.description: List prices in USD. The operation's 402 is the payable quote.

free_now.description: SKUs temporarily free despite their list price.
